body:
The calf stopped drinking after we opened the new feed. Its sister stayed in the back pen on the old sack and still pushed me for breakfast.

I wrote that down before anyone thought to count people. The feed bill was due Friday. I kept telling myself the animal was sulking because I was late.
title: Diary entry

body:
We filled the near trough from the field line and the far one from the well. By dusk the near pen was quiet; the far pen made its usual racket.

I switched the hose myself. My mother asked why I kept a note about water when the cattle needed hay.
title: Notepad page

body:
The bale under the roof was sound. The loose hay left beside the sprayer curled at the edges, and the rabbits would only eat from the roofed bale.

I had promised to sweep both piles before supper. Now the clean one is marked with my old blue string so I can find it in a hurry.
title: Notebook page

body:
My brother took the sacks to the poultry shed on Tuesday. He came back nauseated and slept through Wednesday's milking. The children who stayed in town were well that night.

The invoice sat under the sugar bowl because we still owed for the load. I was angry about the money before I was frightened about him.
title: Diary entry

body:
Our goats grazed the ditch after the field truck passed. The ones shut in the upper pen ate the same hay but never reached the ditch, and they kept their appetites.

I used to complain that the upper gate stuck. That day I was grateful and ashamed of how long it took me to notice why.
title: Letter

body:
Only the flock beside the new grain bin stopped laying. I gave the birds in the yard from the old tin; they made noise all morning and left eggs by noon.

I put the feed scoop on a shelf rather than wash it. It seemed useful to know exactly which bin it had touched.
title: Notepad page

body:
I swept the packing room while the new seed bags were stacked there. By evening my throat burned. My cousin swept the empty stall next door and went to the dance.

We both laughed at my cough at first. I can still see the pale stripe the sacks left on the floor.
title: Diary entry

body: I filled the barrel from the field line after the spray treatment. Those beans withered within days. The row watered from saved rainwater stayed green.
title: Garden notes

body:
Three calves were off their feed in the pen that received the new grain. The others had the same weather and the same night watch but ate from an unopened older sack.

I was supposed to balance the feed bill. Instead I drew the pen divisions on the back of the envelope.
title: Receipt

body:
The lower garden took the muddy overflow from the field. The upper garden stayed dry. A week later the lower leaves had black edges and the upper cabbage was still growing.

I meant to take a photograph for the seed supplier. The camera was full of birthday pictures and I could not bring myself to use the last frame.
title: Letter
